2005.o: Labh Pancham, Dedication Ceremony of Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: Murti-Pratishtha Rituals
The three-day murti-pratishtha rituals at Swaminarayan Akshardham monument commenced on 4 November and culminated on 6 November 2005

The murti-pratishtha rituals for the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Guru Parampara (Gunatitanand Swami, Bhagatji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj) and the deities (Sita-Ram, Radha-Krishna, Lakshmi-Narayan and Shiv-Parvati) in Swaminarayan Akshardham took place over a period of three days: 4, 5 & 6 November. The preliminary pratishtha rituals were performed on smaller murtis that symbolized the murtis of the sanctum in Swaminarayan Akshardham. The yagna rituals were performed at the Bhakti Mandapam on the festival grounds of Swaminarayan Nagar.

4 November 2005 On 4 November 2005 the pratishtha rituals commenced in the presence of Kothari Swami and Tyagvallabh Swami from 8.30 am to 10.30 am. From 10.30 am to 11.30 am Swamishri performed the Vastu Puja rituals, kund puja, yantrastha puja and pithastha dev puja at the kund in Swaminarayan Akshardham. The yagna kund was lit by Swamishri with the torches brought by BAPS youths from Chhapaiya, Bochasan and Chansad. Thereafter the yagna commenced inside the Swaminarayan Akshardham monument. From 4.30 pm to 6.30 pm senior sadhus performed the pithpuja (the base for the murtis) and other rituals which concluded with the arti.

5 November 2005 In the morning the holy water from Narayan Sarovar was brought in 101 pots by 101 female volunteers to the Bhakti Mandapam in Swaminarayan Nagar. Here, from 9.00 am to 12.00 noon, replicas of the murtisof Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Guru Parampara and the deities were placed in small kunds of water (jaladhivaas), grains and ghee. Meanwhile Brahmin pundits poured ghee in the yagna kund to the accompaniment of Vedic mantras. At 10.30 am a traditional, colourful procession was taken out from the Bhakti Mandapam to the Swaminarayan Akshardham monument. Replicas of the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and other deities were placed in decorated floats. More than 350 sadhus participated in the procession. On reaching the inner sanctum of Swaminarayan Akshardham monument, the divinity conferred to the replica of murtis through worship rituals in the yagnashala was transferred through the chanting of mantras into pots filled with water. This holy water was then ritually poured on the original murtisinstalled in the sanctum to imbue them with divinity.

From 4.00 pm to 6.30 pm the juices of different fruits and herbs contained in 49 copper pots were ritually poured on the murtis by Mahant Swami. At 6.30 pm the holy water was ritually poured on the five golden kalashes installed on the monument shikhars. A ritual for protection of the monument was also performed through the chanting of appropriate mantras. Finally a 1½ hour invocation ritual of the natural elements into the murtis was performed.

6 November 2005 : Murti-Ppratishtha at Swaminarayan Akshardham On 6 November the murti-pratishtha ceremony of the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Guru Parampara and the deities in the sanctum of Swaminarayan Akshardham was the climax of all the rituals. Invoking of the Divine into the murtis would inspire reverence in the hearts of devotees when they come for darshan. At 6.45 am rituals at the small yagna kunds, arranged in eight directions on the pradakshina of Gajendra Peeth, began. At every kund a Brahmin pundit and a sadhu performed the preliminary rituals. At 7.00 am senior sadhus started the initial pratishtha rituals in the main monument. Devotees from India and abroad also participated in the rituals. At 9.25 am Swamishri arrived for the main pratishtha rituals. He sat in a chair that was anchored to a special lift that could be manually manoeuvred for the pratishtha rituals of the 11-ft high murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Prior to the pratishtha rituals, Ishwarcharan Swami, coordinator of the Akshardham project, tied an auspicious thread on Swamishri’s wrist and applied a chandlo. Then, Swamishri began to perform the pratishtha rituals. Thereafter Swamishri’s chair was elevated to a height of 11 feet before the face of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The mantras sung by the Brahmin pundits resonated in the sanctum sanctorum of Akshardham. First, Swamishri touched the different parts of the murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, from head to toe, with a gold-tipped darbh stick. Then the invocation of the Divine in every part of the murti (nyas-vidhi) was performed by Swamishri in accordance to the mantras chanted. Swamishri also placed his right hand on the murti’s chest and chanted the Om and Gayatri mantras. This was followed by the ritual opening of the murti’s eyes by Swamishri with the touch of a darbh stick. The same pratishtha rituals were performed simultaneously on the murtis of the Guru Parampara and other deities by the senior sadhus. After offering flowers on the head of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Swamishri held a mirror before the murti’s face. During this ritual the sanctum resonated with the chanting of the Swaminarayan mantra by sadhus and devotees. The pratishtha rituals concluded with the victory calls of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Guru Parampara and the deities. The invocation of the Divine in the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Gunatitanand Swami, Bhagatji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Ram-Sita, Radha-Krishna, Lakshmi-Narayan and Shiv-Parvatiji was complete. Then Swamishri performed pujan of all the murtis. Thereafter an annakut was arranged before the murtis and at 10.10 am Swamishri and the senior sadhus performed the pratishtha arti. This was followed by the ritual offering of flowers (mantra-pushpanjali) to the murtis and then Swamishri blessed the devotees by showering rice grains.

After the auspicious and landmark ceremony, Swamishri was garlanded with a fragrant garland of mogra flowers by Ishwarcharan Swami. Finally, Swamishri blessed the pratishtha occasion, “Yogiji Maharaj’s wish was very strong and powerful. We have seen its realisation today. This place is vast and divine. There is God. See how wonderful the darshan is. We can have the darshan of the avatars. You can see the 500 paramhansas. Wherever you look, you see God, His devotees and muktas. Everything has been done ornately and with attention to detail. Whoever comes inside and does darshan will develop faith in God and become happy. They will become happy in the sense that their inner ignorance and darkness will be destroyed, they will become free from the cycle of life and death, be blessed with the state of brahmarup and attain Akshardham. “Maharaj will not forget those who have served in mind, body and wealth and with feelings of glory. God never forgets those who fold their hands in respect, come with good sentiments or serve, even with lesser means. Whoever has offered services Maharaj will remember him and bless him with Akshardham. “By the grace of God the construction has been done wonderfully. The stone was quarried in Rajasthan. Harshad Chavada has accomplished a great feat. With him was Yogesh Swami who is an engineer. The murtis we are having darshan of have been done by Bhaktinandan Swami. Ishwarcharan Swami and his team have offered their services. Devotees have performed mala, austerities, dhun, prayer and pilgrimage for the creation of this supreme mandir and to please God. “Bhagwan Shriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj are the doers. To accomplish such a huge project is very difficult, but God lifted Mt. Govardhan and the devotees gave their support by raising their staffs. So, what we have done is merely that. The task has been accomplished through His wish and glory. Whoever comes here will be dissolved of evil instincts, be blessed with good feelings and salvation by God.”
From 12.00 noon to 12.45 pm the senior sadhus performed the concluding rituals of homa of the pratishtha yagna.

Akshardham Dedication Ceremony As the winter sun was setting to call it a day, a new era would unfold in its wake. History was in the making in all its eloquent epic divinity and grandeur. Swaminarayan Akshardham was adorned with garlands of flowers and was awaiting the spectacular grand finale opening ceremony. More than 20,000 devotees and volunteers from all over India and the world had taken their seats in the Swaminarayan Akshardham complex. The humongous architectural marvel resonated with years of sacrifice, service, devotion and austerities. Sunday, 6 November 2005 (Labh Pancham V.S. 2062) marked the culmination of Yogiji Maharaj’s vision and dream of a grand mandir on the banks of the river Yamuna. The vision was crystallised by his disciple and successor HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Through his blessings, guidance, and efforts, and the dedication of BAPS sadhus, 7,000 craftsmen and 4,000 volunteers the magnificent Swaminarayan Akshardham complex was ready for its grand opening by the President of India Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh and Opposition Leader Shri Lalkrishna Advani in the holy presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

At 5.00 pm, President Kalam was welcomed at the gates of Akshardham by senior BAPS sadhus. After an initial distant glimpse of the imposing monument, the President saw the boat ride exhibition on India’s glorious culture. Thereafter he viewed the giant screen presentation, Neelkanth Yatra, for five minutes. At 5.30 pm Pramukh Swami Maharaj met President Dr Kalam, Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh, Opposition Leader Shri L.K. Advani and Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Shri B.L. Joshi at the reception centre. Then Swamishri and the guests proceeded along the main avenue towards Akshardham amidst a thunderous welcome from the audience. The dignitaries took their seats in front of the steps, facing the monument.

Then, the podium and the steps of Akshardham erupted in celebration with a dancing troupe of BAPS children dressed in the Indian tricolours rendering the welcome song, “Swagatam”. The air was charged with a traditional flavour of honour and welcome. After the national anthem, Viveksagar Swami spoke briefly about the philosophical meaning and significance of Akshardham. This was then followed by a brilliant exposition on India’s glorious culture and its contribution to the world through nine theme floats. The colourful and lively floats showed how ancient India was the forerunner in agriculture, democracy, science, mathematics, medicine, yoga, education and spirituality. As each float passed by, the Swaminarayan Akshardham monument was appropriately illuminated in different colours.

Then, in his speech, Ishwarcharan Swami described that Akshardham was the fulfilment of Yogiji Maharaj’s dream by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Thereafter, a video film showing the main features of Swaminarayan Akshardham was screened. Swaminarayan Akshardham is a symbol of sacrifice and the labour of love of thousands of sadhus and BAPS volunteers – the fruition of 300 million man-hours of service.

To honour this spirit of Akshardham, over 700 BAPS children and teenagers offered their obeisances through a novel, cultural presentation, “Akshardham Vandate”, that symbolized the five elements of earth, water, air, fire and space. For every element the boys were dressed in appropriate costumes and performed to the special music, song and light effects. The mass participation of over 700 boys performing on the podium and steps of the monument and colonnade was very moving and scintillating. Earth was symbolized through the beating of Indian drums, water was represented by the playing of flutes and pouring of water from auspicious pots into Narayan Sarovar, fire was shown through the ringing of bells, air was depicted through the blowing of conch shells and waving of flags and space was symbolised through the chanting of the Vedic mantra, “Om dhyoho Shantihi”.

At the conclusion of the mesmeric performance Swamishri and the guests climbed up the steps to the main doors of the monument. There, at 6.15 pm the opening ceremony was performed by the President, Prime Minister, Opposition Leader and Lieutenant Governor in the sacred presence of Swamishri. Amidst the chanting of Vedic mantras the President of India Dr APJ Abdul Kalam and Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh untied a golden thread and pushed open the doors to enter the inner sanctum of the Swaminarayan Akshardham Monument with Swamishri. In the morning Swamishri had performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of all the murtis. The dignitaries paid their obeisances to the 11-feet high murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the Guru Parampara and the deities of Sanatan Dharma. They were wonderstruck by the sheer size, and the ornate carvings and divinity of the inner sanctum. When they returned to the main podium of Akshardham, BAPS children were performing a traditional dance on the song, “Mangal Sahajanand Charanraj…” With Akshardham bathed in colourful lights the evening ambience became enchanting, divine and festive.

Mahant Swami honoured the presiding guests with garlands. Thereafter Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh addressed the assembly in Hindi, “I am very happy in participating in the opening ceremony of Akshardham – a beautiful mandir and cultural complex. In the days to come this wonderful mandir and its complex will be counted as one of the principal buildings of Delhi. “Our country unifies diversities but it does not divide people. This is our history and it was also the message of Swaminarayan. He preached regrdless of caste and disapproved of thoughts that divided people. “As I said earlier that this beautiful complex will become unique among the buildings in Delhi. Hundreds of thousands of people and devotees will come to see this from all corners of our country. After being impressed by the attractive murtis here and the peaceful, devotional atmosphere they will definitely leave morally and mentally progressed.” The Prime Minister was honoured with a shawl and presented with a memento before departing from the assembly.
Thereafter an impressive traditional dance by children was performed on the song, “Vande Bharatmataram Akshardham Sanatanam.”

The Opposition Leader, Shri Lalkrishna Advani, spoke gloriously of Swamishri’s feat in creating Akshardham. He said, “The Reader’s Digest has mentioned the London Mandir as one of the wonders in their book 70 Wonders of the Modern World. But if the people of Reader’s Digest had seen the Akshardham in Gandhinagar then they would have definitely mentioned it in their book. …If anyon e comes to see this Akshardham that Pramukh Swami Maharaj has inaugurated today then I have no doubt that they will say that it is The Unique Wonder of the World. A distinct, matchless and amazing creation in our world. It has been rightly said that the thousands of craftsmen, sculptors and Swaminarayan devotees have given 300 million man-hours. The inspiration behind that is the spirit of sacrifice which creates a spiritual revolution in all the devotees. Wherever the Swaminarayan spirit has reached it has made society free from addictions, imbued character and inspired the spirit of sacrifice. The Swaminarayan Akshardham here is a symbol of this sacrifice. “On this occasion today I will say that Yogiji Maharaj, an ideal sadhu of this Swaminarayan tradition, whose dream it was to have Akshardham built on the banks of Yamuna has been accomplished by Pramukh Swamiji. For this great work done by him (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) I congratulate Swamiji and offer my respects with infinite pranams at his feet.”

Thereafter the President, Dr APJ Abdul Kalam addressed the assembly: Power of Ignited Minds “I feel I am in a different world. I am indeed delighted to participate in the dedication assembly of Swaminarayan Akshardham Cultural Complex at New Delhi in the presence of His Divine Holiness Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj. Akshardham Experience “Today, when I entered into the Akshardham Cultural Complex, I get an answer for the question, how can you mix spirituality and social service? How can you separate the two? Those who wish to sincerely serve society must be spiritually pure and only those who are spiritually pure can sincerely serve society and serve the nation. “But who is the creator? The creator we saw in the giant film theatre. A child wading through rivers, climbing over the snowtipped Himalayas, slips and slips and then climbs and climbs, walking across the nation and discovering cradles of India’s civilization. Who is the child? Can you remember the child? Oh! That is the divine child, the child Swaminarayan. The spirit of the divine child entered into Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj. And we see the birth of the Akshardham, the civilizational heritage of India in dynamic form in front of us. Inspirational Leadership “Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj has inspired thousands of people across the country and abroad and brought together the best of the minds for creating a beautiful cultural complex. It has become a place of education, experience and enlightenment. It creatively blends the traditional stone art and architecture, Indian culture and civilization, ancient values and wisdom and the best of modern media and technology. Multiple layers of this complex express the strength of the mind, willpower of the human being, indomitable spirit, flowering kindness, fusion of scientific and medical talent, myriad colours of varied cultures and ultimately the power of knowledge. In essence, it is a dynamic complex with lively images. “Now, Akshardham has happened at the dawn of 21st century with the commitment and dedication of one million volunteers (devotees). What has happened today at Akshardham inspires me and gives me the confid ence that ‘We can do it’. The realization of developed India is certainly possible before 2020 with the millions of ignited minds like you.

Conclusion – Oath for Our Nation’s Prosperity “Now I would like to administer the oath, which I have designed for this occasion with the blessings of His Holiness Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj. Friends, are you ready to repeat with me?
When I see Akshardham, an integrated complex of ancient Indian civilizational heritage, I am inspired and feel proud to be an Indian. I will preserve and nurture it.
Journey through Akshardham gives me the confidence that ‘I can do it, I can do it’. I will apply this in all my actions towards national development.
I realize that nation building is an integrated mission of two components that is spiritual awakening and economic development. I will pursue both simultaneously.

With the foundation of spiritual awakening gained from Akshardham, now my mission will be to enrich the nation hrough commissioning of 1000 Akshardham PURAs (Providing Urban Facilities in Rural Areas) in different parts of the country within the next 5 years under the inspirational leadership of His Divine Holiness Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj.

I will direct all my efforts and knowledge to make India a knowledge society with our ancient civilizational heritage, value system and make India economically strong, prosperous, safe and a peaceful nation within the next 10 years. “My best wishes to all the members of Swaminarayan Akshardham for success in their missions of promoting spirituality and social service. My respects and reverence to Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj and his team. May God bless you.”

Annually the annakut festival is celebrated in all Hindu mandirs throughout the world. Every year Swamishri celebrates this festival in Gondal. A grand feast of a variety of vegetarian foods was arranged before the deities in the mandir and Akshar Deri. Swamishri arrived in Akshar Deri at 11.00 a.m., sang a thal and performed arti. Thereafter Swamishri came to Thakorji in the mandir, where the students of Gondal Gurukul had commenced singing thals. More than 150 devotees were seated beneath the mandir dome before the deities and 250 devotees and sadhus were seated in the mandir pradakshina viewing the bhakti rituals on close circuit TV. After singing five thals Swamishri performed Govardhan puja and arti. Thereafter Swamishri blessed all.
